app_summary: An online shop selling astronomy products, based on the OpenTelemetry Demo. It is built with polyglot microservices (Go, Java, .NET, Python, Node.js, Rust, ...) communicating via gRPC and HTTP behind an Envoy frontend-proxy, with Kafka for asynchronous order processing and Valkey as cart store. Supported Operations: View product catalog, Receive product recommendations and ads, Add item to cart, Checkout with selected items, Currency conversion, Process payment, Generate shipping quotes, Send order confirmation emails

insights: Service 'frontend-proxy' has one backing pod (frontend-proxy-55b6b6c7d9-xqxz5) and that pod is Running — the Service is not missing endpoints at the pod level.

Envoy in the pod reports "loading 13 cluster(s)" and "all clusters initialized" and started its admin HTTP server — cluster configuration was loaded and Envoy initialized successfully in the observed logs.

No upstream connection/cluster errors or repeated gRPC '14 UNAVAILABLE' messages were present in the last ~1000 lines of Envoy logs returned — evidence does not support upstream connectivity failures from this Envoy instance.

Operational warnings observed: a deprecated cluster field ('dns_failure_refresh_rate') is in use, and Envoy logged that there is no configured limit for active downstream connections (recommend configuring resource_monitors.global_downstream_max_connections). These are warnings/operational concerns but not the proximate cause of upstream/unavailable errors in the observed log window.

Overall conclusion: the original hypotheses (no healthy pod endpoints behind the Service, and Envoy emitting upstream/gRPC UNAVAILABLE errors) were disproven by the collected data. The Envoy proxy and its cluster initialization appear healthy; the root cause of any client-visible failures is likely external to this Envoy pod (e.g., upstream service health, network/DNS, kube-proxy/network policy, or client-side issues) and requires further investigation in those areas.
